As of 2020, Schell stated that the project remained in development with a reported budget of around KSh 361 million, but no filming had started.<ref name="nation2020" /> As of 2026, the adaptation has not entered production and is considered stalled.<ref name="wikiMilly">{{cite web |title=My Life with a Criminal: Milly's Story |url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Life_with_a_Criminal:_Milly%27s_Story |website=Wikipedia |access-date=28 May 2026}}</ref>

A film adaptation of the *My Life in Crime* trilogy was announced in 2011, with Canadian-Kenyan director and producer **Neil Schell** attached to the project alongside Janet Kirina of Kirina Productions (in collaboration with Dutch-based Cthrough Productions). The plan was to combine the three books (*My Life in Crime*, *My Life with a Criminal: Milly's Story*, and *My Life in Prison*) into one comprehensive feature film. Nigerian actor **Jim Iyke** was cast as the lead character Jack Zollo, with Kiriamiti himself potentially making a cameo appearance.

The project generated significant local interest and controversy, particularly around the casting of a Nigerian actor in a quintessentially Kenyan story. By 2013–2014, reports emerged that Iyke had been dropped from the role amid discussions over budget and other production issues. As of 2020, Schell confirmed that filming rights had been secured and the project was still in development, with a reported budget of around KSh 361 million, but no principal photography had begun.

As of 2026, the adaptation has not entered production and is considered stalled, with no further public updates from the producers or major Kenyan media outlets.

'''Right Before the 30 Years Curve''' is a 2025 self-help book by South African author [[Emmanuel Sithole]]. Published by Kamvelihle Azania Publisher, the book explores personal growth, mindset, and the challenges faced by young adults before the age of 30.<ref name="Citizen" /><ref name="EkurhuleniNews" />

== Background ==
The book is the seventh published manuscript by Emmanuel Sithole and was written when the author was 23 years old.<ref name="Citizen" /> According to interviews and public commentary by Sithole, the manuscript was inspired by personal experiences and the pressures faced by young people during their teenage years and twenties.<ref name="Citizen" />

Sithole stated that the book was intended to address anxiety related to career expectations, financial pressure, identity uncertainty, and societal expectations surrounding success and adulthood.<ref name="EkurhuleniNews" /> The book was officially released on 26 March 2025.<ref name="EkurhuleniNews" />

== Synopsis and themes ==
The book examines the transitional phase between adolescence and adulthood, presenting it as a formative period that shapes future personal and professional outcomes.<ref name="Scribd" />

Recurring themes in the book include:

* '''The Adulthood Curve:''' Sithole argues that young people should not feel pressured to have their lives fully established before the age of 30.<ref name="Citizen" />
* '''Personal Growth:''' The book discusses emotional resilience, mindset development, discipline, and self-awareness.<ref name="EkurhuleniNews" />
* '''Youth Challenges:''' Topics including financial struggles, career uncertainty, relationships, and social pressure are explored throughout the text.<ref name="Citizen" />
* '''Growth vs. Survival Mindsets:''' The book distinguishes between surviving circumstances and intentionally pursuing long-term growth and development.<ref name="EkurhuleniNews" />

== Reception and media ==
Following its release, the book received coverage across regional and national media platforms in South Africa. In a review published by ''The Citizen'' and the ''Benoni City Times'', journalist Lebohang Pita described the book as a reflective exploration of early adulthood and youth development.<ref name="Citizen" />

Sithole also participated in several radio and media interviews discussing the themes of the book. These included appearances on Alex FM 89.1 during the ''#TheRealDeal'' programme<ref name="AlexFM" /><ref name="AlexPost" /> and an interview feature on [[Ikwekwezi FM]].<ref name="Ikwekwezi" />
